newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN envoy seeks inquiry on murders by Zaire rebels.
newsitem.headline: UN envoy seeks inquiry on murders by Zaire rebels.

text.p: A U.N. human rights investigator has accused Tutsi-led rebels in eastern Zaire of killing thousands of civilians and Rwandan Hutu refugees.

Roberto Garreton, special rapporteur for human rights in Zaire, called for a U.N. commission of inquiry to bring suspects to trial and urged Secretary-General Kofi Annan to provide it with forensic and ballistic experts to excavate mass graves.
The Chilean lawyer's 16-page report includes a list of 40 sites of mass murders allegedly committed by Laurent Kabila's rebels in Northern and Southern Kivu provinces since late last year.
It was submitted on Tuesday to the U.N. Human Rights Commission which is holding its annual six-week talks in Geneva through April 18.

Garreton said it had not been possible to look into alleged crimes committed by the Rwandan Hutu refugees themselves, including the alleged killing of between 500 and 1,500 people at Kitchanga, northwest of Goma, nor abuses by the Zairean army including the deadly shelling of a village on Kisangani road.
"Although the information is frequently inadequate and even contradictory, as a rule the acts denounced actually occurred," he wrote in his report on his March 25-29 trip to eastern Zaire.
"The Rapporteur believes that the events described in this preliminary report cannot go unpunished. What is described here is still going on, with complete impunity."

While conceding that the number of people massacred in some incidents was "undoubtedly exaggerated", he added: "It is indisputable that the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire is far from fulfilling its commitments to respect human rights".

The allegations are based on his preliminary interviews with eyewitnesses or family members of the victims killed during military victories by the rebels who have captured more than a quarter of Zaire with little opposition from government troops.
Garreton, who was mainly in the rebel-controlled border town of Goma, visited three sites in Northern Kivu alleged to hold mass graves -- Kilimanyoka, Kibumba and Katale.
In a forest in Kilimanyoka, he said "various pits covered with stones containing corpses could be clearly seen". A witness who found the graves on January 13 said they held 46 corpses.

Referring to a site in Kibumba refugee camp, where on December 27 remains were found of 37 men who had been shot or killed with axes less than a week before with their hands bound behind their backs, he said: "Of course, many other corpses were found in the camp, but the Rapporteur wishes to highlight those cases where it was quite clear that death was not caused by war."
In Katale, he was told the bodies of 143 people were buried, while in Sake, he was unable to visit two alleged mass graves because Alliance forces had declared military zones.

In the Masisi area of Northern Kivu, where massacres allegedly occurred in Nyakariba and Niabitaba, no escort was provided due to short notice and because of alleged ambushes, he decided not to go. A visit to nearby Matanda was also thwarted.

Garreton cited allegations of rebel soldiers killing civilians in Birambizo, in the Masisi region. "In early January soldiers laid siege to the city, took the children from their families and killed their parents before their eyes. The bodies were piled behind the church and a $3 fee was charged for recovery of each body."
The U.N. envoy quoted Moise Nyarugabo, a top aide to Kabila, as personally telling him that the allegations were part of a "smear campaign" to discredit the Alliance.
But Nyarugabo said the rebels would not oppose a definitive investigation into the alleged killings, according to Garreton.

Garreton urged that a U.N. commission be established to investigate gross violations in eastern Zaire, composed of himself, as well as a member of the U.N. working group on enforced disappearances, the special rapporteur on extra-judicial executions and the special investigator on torture.
